title: Minimum Operations to Make a Rotated Palindrome I
summary: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters, you can perform the following operations any number of times (including zero) and in any order: - Increment: Choose any index i and replace s[i] with the next lowercase English letter.
statement: Given a string s consisting of lowercase English letters, you can perform the following operations any number of times (including zero) and in any order: - Increment: Choose any index i and replace s[i] with the next lowercase English letter. The letter after 'z' wraps around to 'a'. - Left rotate: Move the first character of the string to the end. Determine the minimum number of operations required to make s a palindrome.
constraints: An operation either rotates left once or increments one letter cyclically from z to a.
Return the minimum operations to reach any palindrome.
hints: There are only n distinct rotations, with rotation cost equal to the left-shift count.
For each mirrored pair, either letter can be incremented cyclically until they meet at minimum circular distance.
Evaluate every shift and add pair distances.
Pair edits are independent within a fixed rotation, so their minima sum exactly.
editorial: Pair edits are independent within a fixed rotation, so their minima sum exactly.

tests.explanation: One rotation and one cyclic letter adjustment can form a palindrome in two operations.
The original string is already a palindrome.
